must_know.headline: Russians begin voting in first Duma election since Ukraine invasion, opposition barred
must_know.summary: Voting began Friday in Russia's three-day State Duma election, the first since Moscow's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, with President Vladimir Putin casting the vote as a barometer of support for the war. The Kremlin barred Yabloko, the country's only registered antiwar party, from the ballot in August, while Communist Party candidates seen as likely to draw protest votes were also disqualified or banned. Fuel queues, conscription fears and continued Ukrainian drone strikes are unsettling voters even as United Russia, which won more than two-thirds of Duma seats in the 2021 election, is expected to dominate again.
must_know.why_it_matters: The Kremlin barred Yabloko only after searches for the antiwar party surged fivefold and surpassed those for United Russia itself, suggesting officials were genuinely rattled by the prospect of a protest vote -- and undercutting Putin's framing of the election as a free gauge of public support for the war.

must_know.headline: Bank of Japan raises rates to 31-year high of 1.25%, but yen falls anyway
must_know.summary: The Bank of Japan raised its benchmark interest rate by 0.25 percentage points to 1.25%, the highest level in 31 years and its first hike since June, as it moves away from decades of ultra-low rates to counter inflation running above its 2% target. Two board members opposed the decision, and the yen weakened after the announcement despite hawkish comments from Governor Kazuo Ueda, as investors had expected a faster pace of tightening. The move follows the U.S. Federal Reserve's rate rise earlier this week and comes with the European Central Bank's key rate already at 2.5%.
must_know.why_it_matters: A yen that weakens even as the BoJ hikes suggests markets see Japan still lagging the Fed and ECB on rates; analysts warn that gap could keep pushing the currency down and import costs up, undermining the same inflation fight the rate rise is meant to win.

reporting_varies.angle: Focused on the yen's continued slide despite hawkish rhetoric from Governor Ueda
Framed the hike primarily as an inflation-fighting measure amid rising wages and prices
Emphasized the split vote and internal dissent on the BoJ board

must_know.headline: US approves $24.3bn F-35 sale to Saudi Arabia over Israeli, China concerns
must_know.summary: The US State Department approved a $24.3 billion sale of 48 F-35 stealth jets to Saudi Arabia on Thursday, clearing Riyadh's long-standing effort to acquire the world's most advanced fighter jet and making it the first Arab country approved to operate the plane. The deal, Saudi Arabia's latest major arms purchase since its war with Iran began, still needs to clear a 30-day congressional review; Democratic Representative Raja Krishnamoorthi opposes it, citing US intelligence warnings that China could access F-35 technology through Riyadh's military ties with Beijing. Israel, the only Middle East country currently flying F-35s, has also raised concerns, though Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office says understandings with Washington will preserve its military edge.
must_know.why_it_matters: The sale tests two pillars of long-standing US Middle East policy at once: a legal guarantee that Israel keeps a qualitative military edge over its neighbors, and an effort to keep F-35 technology out of Chinese hands, which US intelligence officials warn Saudi Arabia's expanding military ties with Beijing could put at risk.

reporting_varies.angle: frames the deal as 'controversial,' foregrounding congressional and Israeli objections
reports the approval as a procedural step in a pattern of Saudi arms purchases since the Iran war began
centers the story on Israeli concerns over the deal despite the state department's assurances

must_know.headline: UN panel finds grounds for US war crimes in Iran strikes as Washington admits Iranian delegation to UN
must_know.summary: A UN fact-finding mission said Thursday it has "reasonable grounds to believe" the United States was behind February airstrikes on a school in Minab and a sports complex in Lamerd, saying deaths that included more than 100 children "went beyond negligence"; a separate strike the same day reportedly killed 22 civilians. The findings came as the State Department said it will grant visas for Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi to attend next week's UN General Assembly, even though the war has now passed its half-year mark; their delegation faces travel restrictions and a ban on buying luxury goods.
must_know.why_it_matters: Trump returns to the UN Tuesday to again cast the war as a victory, but he does so with a UN panel accusing his forces of war crimes and, per one analysis, low approval ratings and high gasoline prices that could cost his party control of Congress in November's midterms.

must_know.headline: Russia seizes control of Nestlé, Auchan and Leroy Merlin operations
must_know.summary: Russia placed the local operations of Nestlé, French retailer Auchan and home-improvement chain Leroy Merlin under temporary external administration, according to a presidential decree. It is the first such seizure of Western-owned assets since 2023.
must_know.why_it_matters: The seizure, the first against Western-owned assets since 2023, suggests companies that stayed in Russia no longer have assurance against nationalization, raising the risk calculus for any Western multinational still operating there.

should_know.headline: Canada-EU 'associate member' plan hits reality check over undefined terms
should_know.summary: Canada and the EU face limits to their new partnership after this week's largely symbolic offer to make Canada the bloc's first 'associate member,' Reuters reports, with the Guardian noting uncertainty over what the status would actually mean. The 'associate member' status does not currently exist within the EU, would require agreement from all 27 member states — some of which have previously voiced reservations — and could take years to implement, according to the BBC. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney addressed the European Parliament in Strasbourg this week, saying the proposed alliance was not meant to create a new power bloc.

should_know.headline: Iran's Guard attacks Togo-flagged tanker in Strait of Hormuz
should_know.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps said it attacked and intercepted the Togo-flagged tanker Trend in the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday night after a fire broke out aboard, accusing the vessel of an "illegal passage" and accusing the US military of provoking it. Britain's maritime trade body had earlier flagged a security incident near Khasab, Oman; the crew was reported in good health. Hormuz shipping traffic remained below its 10-day average, with LNG vessels reappearing outside the strait rather than transiting it, Reuters reported.

should_know.headline: Trump to personally greet Xi at Joint Base Andrews ahead of Washington summit
should_know.summary: Trump will meet Xi on the tarmac at Joint Base Andrews when the Chinese leader lands in Washington next Wednesday, a rare airport reception, according to a US official. The summit agenda is expected to cover artificial intelligence, tariffs and a possible extension of the trade-war truce, while China and the US are also discussing announcements to strengthen military-to-military ties. Washington has reportedly delayed new tariffs on excess industrial capacity until after the visit, and executives from BYD, CATL and Xiaomi may travel with Xi.

should_know.headline: France plans €54 billion in spending cuts to curb deficit
should_know.summary: Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said France will cut public spending by €54 billion in the 2027 budget to bring the deficit down to 4.8% of GDP, or 5% including defence spending, from a projected 5.4% this year. He said pensions will not be cut and public benefits will not be frozen, but public sector workers will forgo cost-of-living adjustments, as the government tries to avoid a repeat of the yellow vest protests seven months before the presidential election.

should_know.headline: Boko Haram fighters use AI chatbots to build bombs, Cambridge study finds
should_know.summary: Boko Haram's ISWAP and JAS factions are using chatbots including ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, Meta AI and DeepSeek for bomb-building advice, attack planning and battlefield problem-solving, according to University of Cambridge research based on interviews with 27 former members. Researchers say ISWAP and JAS set up dedicated AI units, including one 23-person team working from a solar-powered room, and that trainers linked to the wider ISIL movement taught senior members to bypass the chatbots' safety restrictions.

should_know.headline: Sweden's Kristersson resigns after narrow election defeat, clearing way for Social Democrats to govern
should_know.summary: Sweden's centre-right Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson announced his resignation on Thursday, after the left-wing opposition won a slim majority in parliament in the country's general election. The move clears the way for the Social Democrats' leader to form a new government.

should_know.headline: Gunman among three killed in Philippines school shooting
should_know.summary: A 16-year-old student shot and killed two classmates before killing himself at Banga National High School in South Cotabato, the Philippines, on Friday, leaving at least eight others injured, four critically. It is the third deadly school shooting in the country since June, following earlier attacks in Tacloban and Zamboanga.

should_know.headline: 37 miners die in Nigerian paramilitary custody, protests erupt in Minna
should_know.summary: At least 37 suspected illegal miners died in the custody of Nigeria's Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) in Niger state, after being detained in raids on gold mines near Minna on September 15-16. Officials initially blamed a disease outbreak, but an intelligence report and a survivor say overcrowding and poor ventilation in the packed cell caused the deaths; the NSCDC's local commandant, Suberu Siyaka Aniviye, has been suspended pending investigation. Protests erupted overnight in Minna, with police firing tear gas, as Niger State Governor Mohammed Umaru Bago declared three days of mourning.

should_know.headline: China Coast Guard rams Philippine vessel on refueling mission
should_know.summary: A China Coast Guard ship intentionally rammed the Philippine vessel BRP Datu Magat Salamat on Friday as it carried fuel to Filipino fisherfolk near Abad Santos (Bombay) Shoal, damaging its railings, stanchions and deck equipment, the Philippine Coast Guard said. No injuries were reported, and the ship was returning to Coron to assess whether it remains seaworthy; the Philippines' National Task Force for the West Philippine Sea condemned the incident as a violation of international maritime law.

should_know.headline: Space Force officials detail US orbital weapons as arms race accelerates
should_know.summary: Air Force Secretary Troy Meink said the US Space Force has deployed "on-orbit space control weapons" capable of defending forces against hostile action, citing threats from China and Russia. Chief of Space Operations Gen. Douglas Schiess said the Space Force "uses active space-based weaponry to support United States national defense," calling the orbital domain increasingly contested amid a wider anti-satellite arms race that has seen China, the US, India and Russia each test such weapons since 2007.

should_know.headline: Spate of alleged Russian plots tests Washington's restraint, experts say
should_know.summary: A series of alleged Russian plots against the West, including a strike on a train that endangered former European leaders and CIA officers, is testing Washington's restraint, according to experts. The attacks form part of a broader pattern that risks a dangerous escalation between Russia and the West, experts say.

should_know.headline: Houthi offensive complicates Trump's Iran war as oil prices soar
should_know.summary: A swift Houthi offensive has sparked fighting and sent oil prices soaring, complicating the Trump administration's war with Iran, according to a Wall Street Journal report examining how the group pulled off the advance.
